title: What a $1,000 website refresh includes—and when you need a rebuild
description: A practical guide to Picshaw's refresh scope, the questions to settle before paying and the signs that a larger rebuild is more appropriate.
author: Picshaw
primaryIntent: Compare a small-business website refresh with a rebuild
intro: The useful question is not whether a website can cost $1,000. It is whether the agreed work solves the problem your business actually has. Here is how to assess Picshaw's refresh option without confusing it with an unlimited rebuild.

sections.title: Start with the published scope
paragraphs: Picshaw's Website Refresh is listed at $1,000. The package focuses on visual redesign, mobile-first presentation, click-to-call and quote forms, search foundations, a clear contact experience and basic analytics. The final page list and deliverables belong in a written scope.

That makes it a starting point for a conversation about an existing site—not a promise that a shop, booking application or complex membership portal can be built for the same price. The broader Growth Site is listed from $2,500 for a 5–10 page website.

sections.title: An illustrative refresh: useful information, difficult presentation
paragraphs: Imagine a local contractor with accurate service descriptions, current contact details and a sensible domain. The problem is that the mobile layout is awkward, project photographs are poorly arranged and the estimate form is hard to find. The business is not changing its services or adding a new booking system.

Our recommendation in that scenario would be to review the existing structure before proposing a wholesale rebuild. The useful work might be a clearer first screen, better service navigation, a working phone link and a shorter enquiry path. This is an illustrative scoping example, not a Picshaw client case study.

sections.title: An illustrative rebuild: the structure no longer fits
paragraphs: Now imagine the same contractor has added a second trade, serves a genuinely different market and wants customers to book appointments through existing operations software. A cosmetic refresh would leave the larger problem unresolved.

The project now needs decisions about page structure, new copy, integration compatibility and testing. That is a reason for a more detailed quote. It is not a reason to stretch an inexpensive headline offer until the scope becomes ambiguous.
bullets: Are the existing services and information still correct?
Can useful pages stay at their current addresses?
Does the business need a new function, or simply a clearer presentation?
Who supplies and approves new copy, photographs and credentials?

sections.title: Clarify the costs that sit around the build
paragraphs: Ask which hosting, domain, software subscriptions and ongoing updates are included, and which are separate. New photography, extensive copywriting, extra revisions and third-party integrations should be discussed before work starts. Do not assume that a one-time build price covers recurring services indefinitely.

Also agree who controls the domain, how the website is handed over, who receives form submissions and what happens when you need a change after launch. A plain-English answer to those questions is more useful than an impressive list of technical acronyms.

sections.title: Protect the useful pages you already have
paragraphs: A redesign can change more than appearance. Google recommends mapping old URLs to their relevant new destinations when addresses change, updating links and monitoring the move. Keep a record of the current pages before replacing the site.
For your review, send the current website address and explain the most important customer action. Picshaw can then recommend the next useful step rather than assume a rebuild is necessary.

title: Why your business website is not appearing in Google: a practical diagnosis
description: Separate crawl access, indexing and ranking problems before buying more content. A step-by-step diagnostic workflow for a small-business website.
author: Picshaw
primaryIntent: Diagnose a business website with little or no search visibility
intro: A site can be online, accessible to Google and indexed while still receiving very few search visits. Start by identifying which problem you have. Otherwise, you may pay for more articles when the useful fix is somewhere else.

sections.title: Check the exact page, not just the business name
paragraphs: Use Google's URL Inspection tool in the verified Search Console property for the website. Inspect the precise URL you care about, including its hostname. The indexed result describes Google's stored view; a live test checks the current page. Those are not interchangeable.

Record the inspected address, the date, whether the page is indexed, any reported access problem and the canonical Google selected when available. A search for the business name can be a useful observation, but it is not a complete indexing diagnosis.

sections.title: When access is the problem
paragraphs: Ask your developer to check the real HTTP response, robots rules, noindex directives, redirects and hosting restrictions. A page that loads for a logged-in owner may not be available to a crawler. The checks should include the actual production hostname rather than only a development preview.
Do not remove access controls from private client work to make a public marketing site discoverable. Keep the two environments separate. Fix the relevant public page, then retest it.

sections.title: When the page is accessible but not indexed
paragraphs: Check whether the page is linked from the rest of the site and whether it duplicates another page. A sitemap helps discovery, but submitting one is not a guarantee of indexing. Google also needs to decide whether to include the page.

Review the substance: does the page help a visitor with a distinct question, or is it a near-copy with a different city name? The practical response may be to improve or consolidate content, not to submit the same thin page repeatedly.

sections.title: A worked example: indexed, but almost no meaningful traffic
paragraphs: During Picshaw's October 9, 2026 review of its own site, URL Inspection reported the homepage as indexed and crawl access as allowed. A live audit also found the apex hostname redirecting to the www version, and no canonical tag on the homepage. The repository had a single public content page, rather than separate pages explaining each service.

Those observations did not prove that a crawler was blocked. Our chosen response was to clarify the preferred URL, add useful service pages and improve internal navigation. This is a record of the diagnosis and proposed response—not a claim that the changes have already produced more traffic.
The lesson for another business is to identify the stage of the problem before buying a remedy. An indexed homepage may need a better explanation of the services, not another indexing request.

sections.title: Define what improvement would look like
paragraphs: Keep a baseline of important indexed pages, relevant search queries, search visits and completed enquiries. Compare the same periods and note when changes went live. A rise in impressions without useful enquiries is a different outcome from a new customer.

For a small local business, we would first prioritise a clear service offer, a working contact path and pages that answer genuine buying questions. Use the data to decide the next content topic rather than publishing every keyword variation.

title: How to make your business website eligible for ChatGPT search
description: Understand ChatGPT's search crawler, check public-page access and improve the information you control without promises of guaranteed AI recommendations.
author: Picshaw
primaryIntent: Understand and check ChatGPT search eligibility for a business website
intro: Start with the part you control: accurate business information on useful pages that search crawlers can access. Eligibility is not the same as being selected for an answer, and no technical setting guarantees a recommendation.

sections.title: Search access and model training are different controls
paragraphs: OpenAI identifies OAI-SearchBot as its search crawler. GPTBot relates to content that may be used for training. The settings are independent: a site can permit search crawling while declining training use. ChatGPT-User handles certain user-triggered visits and is not the control for automatic search inclusion.

sections.title: Ask for evidence that the public page is accessible
paragraphs: OpenAI recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot and requests from its published IP ranges. Check hosting restrictions as well as robots rules; changing a text file does not bypass a firewall.

For a practical audit, record the public URL, response status, robots rules and indexing directives. Ask which tests used an ordinary request and which used a verified crawler address. Merely sending a crawler-like user-agent string is not proof that the real crawler can get through.
bullets: Use the real production URL, including its preferred hostname.
Check that important text and links are present without user interaction.
Keep authenticated drafts and customer previews private.
Record unresolved hosting checks instead of calling the audit complete.

sources.label: OpenAI: search crawler access and IP information

sections.title: Make the business understandable to a prospective customer
paragraphs: Our recommended content review starts with ordinary buying questions: what services are offered, where they are available, who provides them and how someone gets a quote. Put those answers on pages that visitors can navigate, not only inside an image or an interactive widget.

For Picshaw, that means distinct explanations of website redesign, local SEO and AI-search work. A contractor may instead need useful descriptions of its actual trades and coverage area. Neither business needs hundreds of near-identical pages to express the same offer.

sections.title: Prefer specific evidence to confident claims
paragraphs: Our recommendation is to use approved work examples, accurate business details and sources for external claims. Label a concept as a concept. Where you publish results, explain what was measured and over which period.

A practical example is more useful than an unsupported claim that a business is the best in its city. An honest limitation can also help a visitor decide: the website should explain what a package excludes and what needs a separate quote.

sections.title: Do not mistake a technical checklist for guaranteed exposure
paragraphs: Passing an access check means you have addressed that check. It does not mean an assistant will choose your business for every relevant question. Keep a separate record of observed citations, identifiable referral visits and completed enquiries.

Picshaw treats the first engagement as a diagnosis and scoped implementation. Content, distribution and measurement then continue around what the business actually needs. Start with the website you control before paying for a promise about another platform's answers.

title: 12 contractor website checks before you pay for more traffic
description: A free practical checklist for service clarity, mobile contact options, quote requests and genuine evidence on a contractor or home-service website.
author: Picshaw
primaryIntent: Review a contractor website's enquiry path
intro: Open your site on a phone and work through these twelve checks. This is Picshaw's review framework—not a study claiming that each change increases conversions by a fixed amount. Use it to find practical obstacles before buying more visits.

sections.title: Checks 1–3: can a homeowner tell whether you can help?
paragraphs: Read the first screen without relying on what you already know about your business. Someone arriving from a referral or search result should be able to understand the service and the next step.

As an illustrative plumbing example, a heading such as Plumbing repairs and installations is more informative than Solutions you can trust on its own. Add the actual area covered, and mention emergency availability only when it is genuinely offered.
bullets: 1. Name the trade or main service in plain language.
2. State the real service area without implying an office you do not have.
3. Offer a clear next action, such as calling or requesting an estimate.

sections.title: Checks 4–6: does the contact path work on a small screen?
paragraphs: Use a real phone as well as a desktop preview. Tap the menu, scroll to the contact section and try the form without submitting a real job. Check that sticky banners do not hide fields or buttons.
A phone link should open the intended number. A form should explain which information is required and make errors understandable. The visual design is only one part of this check.
bullets: 4. Test the phone link and confirm the displayed number is correct.
5. Check that navigation, text and buttons remain usable without sideways scrolling.
6. Make required form fields and validation messages clear.

sections.title: Checks 7–9: are you helping both the customer and your team?
paragraphs: The form should gather enough information to assess an enquiry without pretending to provide an instant quote when it cannot. The right fields depend on the trade and how the business responds.

For a landscaping enquiry, job type and a basic location may be more useful than a long generic questionnaire. A larger renovation may need a different next step. These are illustrative design choices, not a universal template.
bullets: 7. Explain the main services and any important exclusions.
8. Ask for the job and location details needed to decide whether it is in scope.
9. Give an honest description of what happens after submission.

sections.title: Checks 10–12: can you stand behind the proof and the process?
paragraphs: Project photographs and testimonials should represent real, authorised work. Do not use a mockup as a completed client project, and do not publish a credential or emergency claim simply because it looks reassuring.

Make one controlled test enquiry and confirm it arrives at the correct destination. A success message on the screen is not proof of delivery. Once measurement is available, distinguish completed enquiries from clicks on the submit button.
bullets: 10. Use accurate, authorised photographs, credentials and testimonials.
11. Verify a controlled test enquiry reaches the responsible person.
12. Measure completed enquiries separately from visits and button clicks.

sections.title: Turn the checklist into a short work order
paragraphs: Mark each item as working, needs attention or not applicable. Fix a broken contact path before commissioning another decorative animation. Clarify the offer before creating more versions of the same page.

A simple work order might read: correct the phone link; explain the actual service area; simplify the required form fields; replace an unsupported claim with an approved project example. Record who owns each fix and retest it.
Picshaw can review your existing site and recommend a refresh, a larger rebuild or targeted improvements. The recommendation should follow the problem—not the other way around.
